# Zoning Analysis: 401 N Wabash Ave, Chicago, IL
**PIN: 17101350390000** | Near North Side (Community Area 8)

---

## 1. Zoning District Currently in Effect

This parcel is zoned **Planned Development 835 (PD 835)**, established under City Ordinance No. 13559. This is confirmed by the City of Chicago's official GIS zoning system — you can verify it directly on the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

## 2. Ordinary Base Zoning or Something Else?

**This parcel is NOT governed by an ordinary base zoning district.** It is subject to a **Planned Development (PD)**, which is a site-specific, negotiated zoning instrument established by a unique City Council ordinance (Ordinance 13559). Under Chicago's zoning framework [1], Planned Developments replace standard bulk and density tables with development-specific standards written into the PD ordinance itself. The PD functions as a kind of "mini-zoning code" for this specific site — meaning the FAR, height, setbacks, uses, and other parameters are defined in PD 835's governing ordinance, not in the standard downtown "D district" tables of Chapter 17-4 [1].

> **How to verify:** Search the Chicago City Council's legislative database at [ChicagoCouncil.org](https://chicityclerk.com/legislation-records/) for Ordinance 13559, or request the PD document from the Department of Planning and Development (DPD) at (312) 744-5777.

---

## 3. Key Bulk and Density Standards

Because this parcel is governed by **PD 835** rather than a standard district, **the definitive bulk and density standards — FAR, maximum height, setbacks, minimum lot area — are contained in Ordinance 13559 itself**, not in the Municipal Code's generic tables. The context does not include the text of PD 835's ordinance, so I cannot state those figures with certainty.

What the Municipal Code does say about Planned Developments generally:

- **No maximum building height** applies in "D" downtown districts, and PDs in those contexts are subject to height thresholds that trigger PD review [1]. Upper-story setbacks on **Wabash Avenue** between the Chicago River and Ida B. Wells Drive are restricted: upper-level setbacks are not permitted unless they occur **above 55 feet** [5].
- **Rear setbacks** in DC/DX/DS districts are required only for floors containing dwelling units (minimum 30 feet), with exemptions for DC-12, DX-12, DC-16, and DX-16 [1]. Whether these apply here depends on PD 835's terms.
- **Side setbacks** are not required in DC, DX, or DS districts [1].

**What I could not determine:** The specific FAR cap, maximum height, minimum lot area per dwelling unit, and setback requirements that PD 835 imposes on this parcel. Those are in Ordinance 13559 and are **not in the data provided to me**. You must obtain the PD ordinance text from DPD or the City Clerk.

> **Physical facts on record:** The building is 92 stories, approximately 2,612,396 sq ft of building area on a ~98,019 sq ft land parcel (implying a rough as-built FAR of approximately 26.6 — but this is a derived observation from the property record, not a confirmed zoning entitlement figure). The building was constructed in 2006. This is consistent with Trump International Hotel & Tower, one of the tallest buildings in the Western Hemisphere.

---

## 4. Overlays and Special Designations

The following regulatory overlays apply to this parcel:

- **🏗 Planned Development (PD 835)** — Ordinance 13559. All development on this parcel is governed by the site-specific PD ordinance. Any modification, addition, or new construction requires amendment through DPD and City Council approval [1].

- **🚇 Transit-Oriented Development — CTA Rail** — This parcel is within a CTA TOD area. The nearest CTA rail station is **Grand (Red Line)**, approximately 0.2 miles away. Under the Connected Communities Ordinance, TOD designation enables density bonuses and reduced parking requirements for qualifying projects [2].

- **🚆 Transit-Oriented Development — Metra** — Additionally within a Metra TOD area. The nearest Metra station is **Millennium Station** (Metra Electric Line), approximately 0.37 miles away.

- **🏠 Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone** — This parcel is subject to ARO requirements. Any residential development triggered by a "zoning entitlement" (as defined under [2]) must comply with affordable unit set-aside or fee-in-lieu requirements. In the broader Near North Side community area, the ARO has supported 20 projects totaling 1,010 affordable housing units.

- **No landmark or historic district designation** — This parcel is not in a Chicago Landmark District, is not a designated landmark building, is not in a National Register Historic District, and is not subject to Lakefront Protection Ordinance restrictions.

- **No ADU overlay** — Accessory Dwelling Units are not permitted by overlay here.

- **No Special Service Area (SSA)** applies.

- **Flood Zone X** — FEMA designation "Area of Minimal Flood Hazard." This is **not** a Special Flood Hazard Area; federal flood insurance is not mandated.

- **Brownfield sites nearby** — Several EPA-listed brownfield properties exist in the broader community area, including the **Chicago Hometown Award – Bloomingdale Park Trail** (EPA ID: 110005873260) and **Gateway Park Industrial Complex** (EPA ID: 110039531496). These are not on this parcel, but environmental due diligence is advisable for any ground-disturbing work.

---

## 5. Parking Requirements and Transit-Related Reductions

**I could not determine the specific parking requirements** for this parcel from the data provided. PD 835's ordinance will contain the site-specific parking schedule, which likely departs from standard Municipal Code tables.

Generally, for projects in a CTA TOD area like this one, [2] allows for parking reductions or eliminations for developments that comply with TOD standards (proximity to rail, bike facilities, etc.), subject to Type I Map Amendment or PD review procedures. Because this parcel is already a PD, any parking revision would require PD amendment approval.

> **How to verify:** Obtain Ordinance 13559 from the City Clerk or DPD. You may also contact the DPD Zoning Help Desk at (312) 744-5777.

---

## 6. Maximum FAR and Building Height Allowed

| Parameter | Standard D-District Rule | PD 835 Specific Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Maximum Height | No limit in D districts [1] | **Set by Ordinance 13559 — not available in this data** |
| Maximum FAR | No generic limit in D districts | **Set by Ordinance 13559 — not available in this data** |
| Upper Setbacks on Wabash | Not permitted below 55 ft [5] | Applies unless PD 835 modifies |

The **as-built structure** (92 stories, ~2.6M sq ft) already represents the realized entitlement under PD 835. **Any new project or modification — additions, air rights development, vertical expansion — would require a PD amendment through City Council**, regardless of what a base-district FAR calculation might suggest.
